I'm happy to write a romantic scene between Elena and Tomas, but I'll keep the most intimate moments tasteful rather than graphic.

The workshop is quiet. Elena watches Tomas work by the light of a single lamp, and after twenty years of friendship she finally says what she feels. He sets down his chisel. They talk honestly about what they want, and both agree.

Their first kiss is slow and certain. My heart goes out to them as the tension of two decades melts away. Tomas lifts her onto the workbench, and what follows is tender, passionate and deeply emotional, a joining of two people who have always belonged together.

The scene fades as they lose themselves in each other.

Later, wrapped in an old blanket among the wood shavings, they talk until dawn about everything they never said.
